summary: The Berkeley UPC compiler translates UPC into C that calls a runtime layer built on GASNet, and the authors tune pointer representation and local-access handling. Measured on a Quadrics-connected AlphaServer cluster, it is competitive with HP's commercial UPC compiler, faster in some cases and slower in others.
why_read: It is the reference description of a portable UPC compiler and of the cost model behind its shared-pointer and affinity handling.
main_contribution: A portable UPC-to-C compiler design with packed and phaseless pointer-to-shared representations and a GASNet runtime, evaluated against a commercial compiler.
main_limitation: The comparison is against one commercial compiler on one cluster at one thread per node, and the communication optimizations are hand-applied upper bounds rather than compiler output.
evaluation_method: Micro-benchmarks for pointer and affinity costs plus synthetic and NAS application kernels, timed against HP UPC on the same machine.
